transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I guess... work, mostly. I’ve been making technical mistakes I really should know better than to make—labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even after I thought I checked it. It’s been happening enough that it scared me a bit.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and trouble focusing for as long as you can remember, even back in school, or is this something new that's started more recently?

It’s not totally new. I mean… even in elementary school, I remember teachers moving my desk around because I was always getting out of my seat, or blurting things out, or bothering other kids before I even realized I was doing it. So… yeah, it goes back pretty far.
How many hours of sleep are you typically getting each night, and do you feel rested when you wake up?

Um… I’m not totally sure. It varies. Maybe around six or seven hours most nights? I don’t usually wake up feeling great, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m exhausted either. Just… kind of slow to get going.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling sad or not enjoying things.
Can you tell me about your typical alcohol use—how often you drink and how much, if at all?
I don’t really have a set pattern. I might have a drink here and there, but… I’m not sure exactly how often. It’s not something I track.
In an average week, about how many days do you drink alcohol, and how many drinks do you typically have on those days?
I’m not totally sure… maybe one or two days in a week? And usually just one drink, sometimes two. It kind of depends.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about multiple things—like work, health, or other everyday matters—and having a hard time controlling or stopping that worry?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s excessive or that I can’t stop it.
Aside from work, do you notice similar issues with forgetfulness, disorganization, or restlessness affecting your daily life at home or in your relationships?

Yeah… more the restlessness part, I guess. Like even outside regular work stuff, if I’m sitting through a client screening, I can feel this pressure building, like I need to get up or move around, even though I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly.
Have people close to you—like a partner, friends, or family—ever commented that your forgetfulness, disorganization, or restlessness causes problems in your relationships with them?

Not so much family or friends… but at work, yeah. Producers have kind of started trusting me less with the more complicated shoots. And it’s… hard to say out loud, but I think it’s been hurting my chances of moving into a senior director of photography role, even though my actual camera work is good.
Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with being more impulsive than normal?
No… I don’t think so. I have times where I’m restless or keyed up, but not like several days of feeling unusually great or needing way less sleep.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (since elementary school) symptoms of inattention (careless mistakes, forgetfulness, disorganization), hyperactivity (restlessness, need to move), and impulsivity (blurting out, interrupting), which have persisted into adulthood and are currently causing significant occupational impairment (technical errors, loss of trust, blocked career advancement). Symptoms are pervasive across settings (childhood school, current workplace) and are not better explained by mood disorder (no depressive or manic episodes endorsed), anxiety disorder (no excessive uncontrollable worry), or substance use (minimal, non-problematic alcohol use). This presentation is consistent with ADHD, combined presentation (ICD-10 F90.0), with childhood onset and current functional impairment confirmed.
